raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Why

`test_fs_tiering_offloading` sometimes fails with AssertionError: No CPU stored events received. MockSubscriber.get_new_cpu_stored_events() only polls for 1s, then returns empty instead of waiting for the drain deadline. With a real fs tier, disk I/O can delay the CPU BlockStored event past 1s, causing flakiness. Test-only issue, not OffloadingConnector.

## Fix
Keep polling until _EVENT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT if no CPU stored event has been seen. After one arrives, return on the next idle poll.

detail.body:
## Why

`test_fs_tiering_offloading` sometimes fails with AssertionError: No CPU stored events received. MockSubscriber.get_new_cpu_stored_events() only polls for 1s, then returns empty instead of waiting for the drain deadline. With a real fs tier, disk I/O can delay the CPU BlockStored event past 1s, causing flakiness. Test-only issue, not OffloadingConnector.

## Fix
Keep polling until _EVENT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT if no CPU stored event has been seen. After one arrives, return on the next idle poll.
detail.title: [XPU] [CI] Fix flaky get_new_cpu_stored_events in offloading connector tests

files.patch:
@@ -102,10 +102,18 @@ def get_new_cpu_stored_events(self) -> list[BlockStored]:
         poll_ms = _FIRST_EVENT_POLL_MS
         deadline = time.monotonic() + _EVENT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT
         while time.monotonic() < deadline:
-            events = dict(poller.poll(poll_ms))
+            remaining_ms = max(1, int((deadline - time.monotonic()) * 1000))
+            events = dict(poller.poll(min(poll_ms, remaining_ms)))
 
             if events.get(self.sub) != zmq.POLLIN:
-                return cpu_stored_events
+                # Once at least one CPU stored event has been seen, a single
+                # idle poll means the burst has drained, so return early.
+                # Before that, keep retrying until the deadline: publishing
+                # can be delayed (e.g. by real disk I/O in fs-tiering
+                # secondary tiers) well past the first poll window.
+                if cpu_stored_events:
+                    return cpu_stored_events
+                continue
 
             topic_bytes, _, payload = self.sub.recv_multipart()
